courses.course: Ph.D. in Computer Applied Technology, School of Computer Science

timeline.summary: Researching and prototyping how hierarchical reasoning-and-control mechanisms from embodied AI can be transferred to Game AI, targeting cross-scenario generalization, complex-scene reasoning, low-latency action execution, and natural, believable human-like behavior.
highlights: Contributed to a hierarchical high-level/low-level fast-slow architecture: the deliberative high-level module handles semantic understanding, long-horizon planning, and complex decision-making, while the reactive low-level module supports low-latency action selection and execution, enabling the architecture to balance cross-scenario generalization, complex-scene reasoning, and runtime responsiveness.

Systematically reviewed external data samples, iterated multiple versions of data-collection standards and quality-acceptance criteria with the team, and conducted acceptance and quality checks on the initial delivered batch to establish a consistent data foundation for subsequent experiments.

Researched structured representations of game scenes and assets and developed a scene representation encoder that converts structured scene and asset information into inputs consumable by multimodal models, replacing the agent-facing RGB observation stream and exploring deployment without an additional RGB rendering pass.
Set up an initial evaluation environment and validation workflow for early assessment of model behavior, action execution, and deployment feasibility across representative scenarios.

timeline.company: Beijing Innovation Center of Humanoid Robotics
timeline.summary: Researching pretraining and long-horizon modeling for embodied world models, spanning memory systems, World Action Models, and data infrastructure for egocentric human-hand and robot data.
highlights: Designed an embodied memory system to mitigate temporal inconsistency and memory drift in long-horizon video generation.
Built a World Action Model on top of the memory system to improve action planning and generation consistency for long-horizon robotic tasks.
Investigated how to jointly incorporate egocentric human-hand and robot data into world-model pretraining to improve pretraining performance.
Built separate data-validation and cleaning pipelines for egocentric human-hand and robot data, deeply integrating both into the company's existing data-processing workflow.

timeline.summary: Conducted research in the Joint Lab (Simplexity Robotics & PKU) on VLA deployment in real mobile manipulation scenarios, spanning task understanding, action generation, execution feedback, and robot-system deployment.
highlights: Systematically optimized whole-body control and mobile-manipulation coupling within a fast-slow dual-system architecture centered on latent-space reasoning, improving the stability and consistency of action generation under complex motion states.
Explored robot proprioception modeling by integrating joint-torque and other physical-state signals.
Introduced Human-in-the-Loop reinforcement learning with online human feedback to improve real-world adaptability and robustness.

Contributed substantially to the end-to-end design and iteration of two generations of lightweight egocentric hand-data collection gloves. Both generations used a ZED 2i for the primary ego view and dual wrist-mounted Insta360 GO 3S cameras, with a companion Unity application for capture visualization and three-camera timestamp synchronization.
For Gen 1, used magnetic localization for wrist-pose estimation and a multi-IMU configuration for finger-joint capture, completing the first integrated glove and data-collection system.

For Gen 2, replaced magnetic wrist localization with SLAM and reduced the IMU count; motion retargeting and rigorous accuracy validation preserved finger-joint localization accuracy while significantly lowering hardware cost and mitigating wrist-tracker dropouts in challenging positions and orientations.
Incorporated multi-task, multi-view human-hand data collected with the gloves into VLA pretraining and downstream training, improving generalization to out-of-distribution scenarios.
Deployed and operated Galaxea R1 Lite and Franka Emika Panda robots end-to-end, covering real-robot data collection and cleaning, model training, testing, and validation.
Collaborated with the hardware team on bring-up and debugging of Simplexity Robotics' in-house i7 Pro platform, including its mobile base and dual-arm system.
Designed and fabricated multiple custom 3D-printed robot components for the team's hardware development, enabling rapid structural iteration and real-system debugging.

roles.title: Research Intern, Embodied Multimodal LLM Research Center

timeline.summary: Contributed to the open-source RoboBrain 1.0/2.0 projects and the RoboMIND benchmark, and co-developed AC-DiT, an end-to-end VLA method for mobile manipulation that achieved state-of-the-art performance across multiple benchmarks.
highlights: Co-built RoboBrain 1.0/2.0 to improve LLM/VLM spatial understanding, temporal modeling, and long-chain reasoning.
Co-developed AC-DiT, an end-to-end VLA method that achieved state-of-the-art performance across multiple mobile-manipulation benchmarks.

Contributed to building RoboMIND (RSS 2025), a standardized multi-embodiment robot-manipulation dataset and benchmark comprising 107K demonstration trajectories across 4 robot embodiments, 479 tasks, and 96 object classes, with 5K real-world failure demonstrations annotated with their causes and an Isaac Sim digital-twin environment.

Performed hardware bring-up, system debugging, and real-robot data collection for the AgileX Mobile ALOHA platforms and a RealMan compound single-arm lifting robot. The AgileX systems included an integrated Cobot Magic robot and a split-configuration ALOHA; the RealMan platform features an RM65-B-V arm, 900 mm of vertical travel, a 5 kg payload, a compact 505 mm circular base, and autonomous SLAM navigation.
Built cross-simulator mobile-manipulation datasets and evaluation benchmarks spanning SAPIEN, MuJoCo, CoppeliaSim, and Isaac Sim.
Developed data-collection pipelines across these simulation environments with support for VR and SpaceMouse teleoperation.
Led construction of robot digital assets across simulators, including 100+ objects and 10+ scenes.
